title: Fable 5.2 was the first model capable of doing reliable sprite to skeleton
author: GeorgiaWitness1
selftext:
Have been months on this. 

The previous models were not capable of doing this. This was the first run and workflow that i was able to do, still a lot to be done, but im happy with the results. 

Fable 5.2 is able to use Opus/Sonnet with a base image and then a video generation, i use Omni 1.2 just because it's cheap (paid the flow sub for this), and use it to build the spine as good as possible. 

Now i can change armor and weapons and have a better FPS experience. 

I put this in a repo, [https://github.com/enoch3712/spine-hero-skill](https://github.com/enoch3712/spine-hero-skill) and i hope it can help you guys. 

**Disclosure**: I used [spine](https://esotericsoftware.com/), is not expensive for the basic license so i decided to keep it.

comments.author: xens999
comments.body: Cheers, sprite animation is surprisingly difficult on these models. I'm using Codex right now (might switch to Claude soon if they don't put out a better model soon). I'm doing pokemon sprites at the moment and trying to update the old very pixelly sprites into something better looking and man is it tough to get the results you want. comments.author: NightMailworks
comments.body: Nice.  I've been using meshy to generate rough 3D models, rigging those, baking out 8-way facing sheets with a shader that accentuates features (e.g. using strong rim lighting component), and then having gpt-image-2 do paintovers on a solid color that can be chromakey removed.  The model also lets me bake out depth and normals for better dynamic lighting, and the rig can be used for attachments like weapons, etc.  What I learned is that you can't just image generate every frame or you get lots of "boiling" artifacts.  Instead, I've had most luck generating keyframes and tweening using traditional 2D animation techniques.
